sentences: For a relation, an algorithm may output any answer satisfying the input-output specification rather than one uniquely determined value.
This makes the precise convention for reducing error more consequential than it is for ordinary decision problems.
The source compares FBPP with a version requiring negligible error and gives a relation separating the classes in one direction.
The remaining question is whether an inclusion holds in the other direction or whether the two classes are incomparable.
An answer would clarify which amplification intuitions remain valid when success means producing an arbitrary valid output.
